name: Behind-the-meter gas generation for data centres
aliases: BTM gas power for data centres
onsite gas generation for data centres
principle: Data centres site gas turbines or large reciprocating gensets on their own side of the meter to escape multi-year grid-interconnection queues and hedge power-price volatility. GE Vernova markets configurations from a 20-30 MW aeroderivative unit up to 3 GW campuses, with mobile TM2500 units installable in about 14 days and heavy-duty 7HA.03 units at 430 MW; the Chevron/Engine No.1/GE Vernova 'power foundry' programme targets 4 GW of co-located capacity by 2027. Caterpillar restarted 10 MW-class genset production and is investing USD 725 million to expand large-engine capacity for data-centre demand.

advantages: Escapes grid interconnection queues measured in years
Price hedge and long-term cost predictability for operators
Mobile aeroderivative units bridge to permanent capacity
limitations: Combustion emissions and permitting (NOx, CO2) constrain siting
Fuel-supply agreements and gas-price exposure shift risk to the operator
Turbine delivery backlogs now run to years for large heavy-duty frames
